purpose: This medication is used to lower high phosphate levels in your blood if you have chronic kidney disease and are on dialysis. When your kidneys are not working well, phosphate can build up in your body and cause serious problems like weak bones and heart issues. This medicine helps keep your phosphate levels in a safe range.
how_it_works: Sucroferric oxyhydroxide works by binding to phosphate in the food and drinks you consume while it is still in your stomach and intestines. Once it grabs onto the phosphate, it prevents your body from absorbing it into your bloodstream. The phosphate then leaves your body through your stool instead of building up in your blood.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dark or discolored stools, which is normal and harmless. Some people also experience diarrhea, nausea, constipation, or an upset stomach. These side effects are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have too much iron in your body or certain conditions that affect how your body handles iron, such as hemochromatosis. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as this medicine can interfere with how some drugs are absorbed. Always take it with meals as directed, and keep your doctor informed about any new or worsening symptoms.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 3 chewable tablets taken by mouth with meals each day, meaning 1 tablet with each of your 3 main meals. The tablets should be chewed thoroughly and not swallowed whole. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your blood phosphate levels, typically ranging from 3 to 6 tablets per day.
